title: By night to Jerusalem
hook: he is carried by night from Mecca to the Far Distant Place of Worship, and leads the prophets in prayer (17:1; Muslim)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the angel of the mountains, and a hope for children not yet born. Your line was: hope for their children.

"Glorified be He Who carried His servant by night." That is how surah seventeen opens in Pickthall's translation, and the surah is known as al-Isra, the night journey. After the losses, after Ta'if, after the cloud and the mountains, the sirah turns to a single night. He is in Mecca, at the sanctuary, on an ordinary night. By morning he will say he has been to Jerusalem and back, and the town will have something new to mock. Today's word: Isra.
screen: `GLORIFIED BE HE WHO CARRIED HIS SERVANT.` → `AFTER THE LOSSES.` → `ONE NIGHT.`

segments.voice: Here is the whole opening line in Pickthall: "Glorified be He Who carried His servant by night from the Inviolable Place of Worship to the Far Distant Place of Worship." The Inviolable Place is the sanctuary at Mecca. The Far Distant Place, in Arabic al-masjid al-aqsa, Muslims understand as the holy place in Jerusalem, and Sahih Muslim names it Bayt al-Maqdis, the House of holiness. Notice the verb: not that he traveled, but that he was carried. Muslim's report from Anas fills in the scene. A white animal called al-Buraq is brought, smaller than a mule and bigger than a donkey, its stride reaching as far as its eye can see. He rides it to Jerusalem, ties it at the ring where the prophets used to tie their mounts, and goes in and prays. Jibril brings him two cups, one of wine and one of milk. He chooses the milk, and Jibril says: you have chosen the fitra, the natural way. Another report in Sahih Muslim adds the detail that gives us today's line. He found himself among a gathering of prophets, and when the time for prayer came, he led them. Picture that row: men whose stories this path has told, standing shoulder to shoulder, and the man just driven out of Ta'if at the front. Muslim scholars have discussed whether the journey was in body and spirit or in a vision, and the sources record that discussion. What the tellings share is the night, the distance, and the row.
screen: `CARRIED BY NIGHT.` · `TO THE FAR DISTANT PLACE OF WORSHIP.` · `AL-BURAQ, MILK OVER WINE.` · `HE LEADS THE PROPHETS IN PRAYER.` · then, large: `THE PROPHETS IN ONE ROW.`

segments.voice: Let your attention travel the way the verse does: from where you are, across distance, to an old city of stone. Then picture a row of people at prayer, shoulder to shoulder, nobody pushed to the back, with unexpected faces beside you. If you pray, you can recite the opening of surah seventeen, or simply say subhan Allah, glory be to Allah, as the verse begins; if not, just hold the picture of the row.
Isra: the night journey. In surah seventeen he is carried by night from Mecca to the Far Distant Place of Worship, and in Muslim, he leads the prophets there in prayer. Today's word.
Your line: the prophets in one row. Carried by night, and placed at the front. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Some Muslim communities remember the Isra and Mi'raj on a night in the month of Rajab, and surah 17 is also called al-Isra after its opening verse.

chat.says: What happened on the Isra, the night journey?
options: Carried by night from Mecca to Jerusalem, he led the prophets in prayer.
He and his companions left Mecca for good and settled in Medina.
He walked alone to Jerusalem over many nights to pray at its gates.
